problems.issue: Cystic renal disease is inadequately represented: polycystic kidney dysplasia, enlarged kidneys and hypertension are entirely absent despite reporting rates of 95%, 70% and 80% in R1-train. The simulation instead emphasizes a generic nephronophthisis presentation, potentially teaching the wrong NEK8 renal phenotype.

Example 3 combines polydipsia with hypodipsia without temporal context and lacks a defining renal finding. Example 2 includes short sperm flagella, an unusual and age-dependent finding requiring specific justification. These records introduce contradictory or poorly supported associations.

Median age 6 years substantially exceeds R1-train's 0.2 years and may underrepresent severe infantile NEK8-associated disease. Childhood nephronophthisis remains plausible; gene-level R1 cases may represent a different disease spectrum.

Example 1 contains only end-stage kidney disease and drug allergy, providing no disease-specific renal description. Retinal degeneration in 13% also warrants support rather than being assumed from other nephronophthisis syndromes.

summary: Renal failure, polyuria, polydipsia, anemia and growth impairment are plausible, and the sex distribution is acceptable. However, absent cystic/enlarged-kidney phenotypes and problematic example records make this simulated cohort implausible overall. Missing literature prevalence data and potentially mixed NEK8 phenotypes limit exact calibration.
